title: 10 Creative Ways Museums Can Use Food to Connect with Audiences
content:
Incorporating food into museum programming offers a unique and dynamic way to engage audiences by connecting cultural heritage, history, and art through a universal human experience. Here are ten innovative strategies, each illustrated by institutions that have successfully implemented them:

Themed supper clubs offer immersive dining experiences inspired by museum exhibitions. The Garden Museum in London has organized supper clubs featuring menus crafted around specific exhibitions, blending culinary arts with storytelling to create unforgettable evenings.

Workshops teaching traditional cooking methods can transform museums into living history centers. The Food Museum in Suffolk, UK, runs seasonal classes where participants learn to make dishes like Christmas mince pies, offering hands-on insights into culinary traditions.

Exhibitions dedicated to food can explore its cultural, historical, and social significance. The Southern Food & Beverage Museum in New Orleans showcases the culinary traditions of the American South, illustrating how food shapes cultural identity through historical artifacts and multimedia displays.

title: From pilot to policy: what Europe’s new culture declaration means for museum health and well-being
content:
In June 2026, the EU’s three main institutions put culture’s benefits for health and wellbeing into a shared political commitment for the first time. For museums running wellbeing programmes, it marks the moment the work moved from pilot projects into policy.

For more than a decade, museum health and wellbeing work has grown from the ground up. A dementia programme here, a social prescribing pilot there, a slow-looking session for NHS staff somewhere else. The evidence has built steadily, but the work has often depended on a passionate team, a short-term grant and a sympathetic director.

2026 looks different. On 18 June, the European Parliament, the European Commission and the Council of the EU signed a joint declaration called Europe for Culture – Culture for Europe. Among its commitments is a pledge to promote the positive effects of culture on health and wellbeing.
